scope: Current production query design, proposed modular query families, GitHub repository discovery, multilingual recall, intelligence-tool discovery, compute-tool discovery, and incumbent change detection.

limitations: This is not a measurement of the entire public internet.
Topical relevance was manually judged from repository identity and search result metadata.
Official status, license, security and suitability still require second-stage verification.
Tavily and Exa were assessed from the latest production report rather than re-run in this test.

latest_production_run.conclusion: The current production workflow is stable but primarily discovers webpages and OpenAPI catalog references. It is not yet a functioning four-radar system.

sample_metrics.multilingual_result: Chinese produced moderate recall, French low precision, Japanese and Arabic produced zero results in local-language-only tests.
sample_metrics.interpretation: Short platform-specific capability queries are materially better than the current global five-axis conjunction. Topic recall is acceptable in English, but official-source precision and multilingual recall require a second-stage verifier and mixed-language expansion.

incumbent_change_detection_spot_checks.finding: Recent commits exposed a version bump to 3.4.0 and a new npm publish workflow, demonstrating that GitHub commit monitoring can detect capability and distribution changes.

Recent commits included dependency updates and removal of the AutoGluon integration and BEST quality tier, demonstrating that commit-level monitoring can detect both maintenance and breaking capability removals.
Repository is public and not archived; commit history shows the v1.1.0 release, demonstrating release fingerprinting but also the need for stale-maintenance thresholds.

main_blind_spots: Only nine explicit local-language keyword groups
No dedicated production compute-tool keyword planner
No production capability fingerprint and diff pipeline
No systematic official-organization and official-domain verifier
No coverage-gap-driven query prioritization in the current executor
Insufficient protocol and format coverage for scientific, geospatial and streaming ecosystems
Search-engine and registry adapters described in policy but not all implemented

required_changes: Replace the single five-axis conjunction with platform-specific query families containing one primary capability and at most one or two optional constraints.
Use two-stage retrieval: broad candidate discovery followed by official, license, maintenance, security and free-mode verification.
Build a dedicated compute-tool keyword taxonomy and registry adapter set.
Use mixed-language expansion: local language + English synonyms + transliteration + country/TLD or official organization signals.
Add missing languages and regional variants based on coverage gaps rather than a fixed nine-language list.
Add a gold-set benchmark with known sources and tools across regions, languages and capability families; measure recall, precision and accepted-candidate yield every release.
Implement capability fingerprints and added/removed/changed/breaking diffs for existing APIs, MCPs, SDKs, packages, models and datasets.
Prioritize searches from uncovered or stale coverage cells and retain negative evidence to prevent repeated low-yield queries.
Use registries before search engines and reserve at least half of free search quota for user tasks.
verdict: The keyword universe is broad enough to form a strong taxonomy, but the current combinations and production wiring are not sufficient for global full coverage. Search quality is good for short English capability queries, moderate for regional/domain queries, and weak or unstable for local-language-only queries. The current production workflow should not be described as full coverage until modular planning, multilingual expansion, registries, four machine libraries, change fingerprints and recurring benchmark tests are operational.
